title.narrative: Mauritania First Reforms for Inclusive and Sustainable Growth DPF

description.narrative: The development objectives of First Reform for Inclusive and sustainable Growth Development Policy Financing (DPF) Program for Mauritania are the following: (i) strengthening property tax collection and the regulatory framework for private investment, (ii) building human capital and skills for jobs, and (iii) accelerating inclusive access to affordable and sustainable energy services. The DPF series supports Mauritania's development ambition highlighted in the 2016-2030 SCAPP and its climate commitments. This strategy is built around three pillars: (i) structural transformation to accelerate the diversification of the economy; (ii) promoting human capital development; and (iii) strengthening governance in all its dimensions. The DPF program demonstrates alignment with the upcoming CPF covering FY2026-FY2030 by supporting several of its key outcomes. It is aligned with the WBG's Maximizing Finance for Development (MFD) approach, and private investment generated through the project is categorized as Private Capital Enabling (PCE). This operation aligns with the mitigation and adaptation and resilience goals of the Paris Agreement. The DPF reform program adheres to the country's climate commitments as outlined in the NDC, based on the World Bank's Sahel Climate Change Development Report (CCDR-2022).

comment.narrative: On track. According to TOFE data, property tax revenues increased by 40.3 percent in 2025 (from 0.17 to 0.22 percent of GDP), consistent with ongoing progress in the digitization of land administration and the expansion of property tax coverage in major urban centers. title.narrative: Percentage of health facilities with uninterrupted availability of essential medicines during the last three month

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. The share of health facilities with no stock-out of essential medicines during the preceding three months reached 45 percent as of March 2026, exceeding the target. This progress is consistent with implementation gains under the INAYA project (P179558), including the full rollout of performance-based financing across targeted health facilities and the regular conduct of verification and payment cycles. However, progress on this indicator may be affected by higher international freight and import costs and potential disruptions to delivery timelines for imported pharmaceutical inputs due to the Middle East conflict. The team is monitoring external supply and price developments and engaging with counterparts on mitigation measures to protect the continuity of essential medicines supply.

comment.narrative: On track. Installed renewable energy capacity reached 215 MW. Since 2024, renewable energy deployment has been supported by the attribution of new licenses, including one license for a 60 MW hybrid IPP project (solar and wind), as well as 3 licenses to private operators for the development of 12 hybrid plants across isolated grids, with solar accounting for more than 80 percent. The regulatory framework is being implemented, with the Regulatory Authority ensuring application of the decree on licensing criteria and priority grid access. However, effective priority grid access remains contingent on finalizing the transport operator license (currently under preparation, with its terms of reference already approved)

title.narrative: People provided with access to electricity (millions)

comment.narrative: On track. Access to electricity increased moderately, from 2.70 million to 2.85 million people, of which around 48 percent is estimated to be provided through renewable energy sources. Key instruments to operationalize the Rural Electrification Fund have been finalized (three decrees and one implementing order) and will be submitted to the Government by October 2026.

Value of investments generated under the new investment code

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. Approved investments under the revised investment code reached approximately US$120 million in 2025, across 19 projects, above the end target of US$108 million. The investments are distributed across the structural, intermediate, and SME regimes, and associated with the expected creation of approximately 939 direct jobs. However, these figures reflect approved investment intentions rather than realized investments. The team is engaging with the authorities to assess whether a systematic follow-up mechanism is in place to track approved projects and verify the extent to which declared investments are effectively materialized.

Technical and commercial losses in the electricity sector

comment.narrative:
No updated data are available yet. The indicator will be updated once new data become available.
The decree introducing activity-based accounting for SOMELEC has been adopted, and restructuring has begun with the appointment of management for separate entities (transport/production, distribution/commercialization, and rural electrification). The authorities are preparing licenses with associated performance requirements for each activity. However, delays in asset inventory and financial model development have slowed progress. The Government granted a 24-month moratorium to complete the restructuring, extending the timeline to March 2028.

TVET graduates employed within six months of graduation

comment.narrative: No updated data are available at this stage on TVET graduates employed within the past six months. The Labor Market Information System (SIMEM) has been established and is operational, with high-frequency broad labor market data being collected and quarterly reports produced by ANSADE (most recent: Q4 2025) - including labor force participation, the employment-to-population ratio, unemployment rates (overall, for youth, and for women), sectoral distribution of employment, and labor underutilization. The team expects to update these indicators in the October 2026 ISR.

Rate of deliveries assisted by qualified personnel

comment.narrative: On track. Progress on skilled birth attendance remains limited. Performance-Based Financing (PBF) - the primary mechanism for incentivizing health facility performance - has been institutionalized through a decree (DPO1), but implementing regulations have not yet been finalized, delaying full operationalization. The rollout of community-based PBF has faced delays due to shortages of community health workers. To address this, authorities have launched a joint implementation plan with the Ministry of Health and UNICEF, and nearly 300 community health workers have been trained and equipped to date. Progress toward the target is also supported by the World Bank INAYA project (P179558). Achieving the 85 percent target by December 2028 will require significant acceleration.
